atlas-vn.0097: Vietcombank’s outstanding-graduate track requires IELTS 7.0, TOEIC 785, TOEFL 550 or CEFR C1 and an office-IT certificate; BIDV has FDI-client tracks in Korean and Chinese.
atlas-vn.0098: The British Council report says English is particularly in demand in financial services.
atlas-vn.0099: Grant Thornton Hanoi asks for fluent English in reading, writing, speaking and listening, takes the application and CV in English, and sets an English test for those exempt from its technical test.
atlas-vn.0100: FPT Software’s fresher post asks for good reading and communication English, equivalent to TOEIC 700+; ITviec offers its pages in English and Vietnamese.
atlas-vn.0101: In the 2018 British Council survey, 77% of foreign companies and 76% of conglomerates said English skills were particularly important, and 87% of employers agreed that jobseekers lack language skills; Vietnamese is the language of local firms.
atlas-vn.0102: Youth (15–24) unemployment was 8.86% in the first quarter of 2026 against 2.23% for all working-age people in the second quarter; it was 8.6% for 2025 and 9.04% in the fourth quarter. About 1.4 million young people, 10.2% of the youth population, were neither working nor in education or training. We found no graduate-specific figure or return-offer rate for Vietnam.
atlas-vn.0103: VnEconomy (August 2026) reports that around 70% of university graduates still need retraining after entering the workforce, and that employers value communication, teamwork and adaptability; the 2018 British Council report says graduate unemployment and underemployment are high because the education system struggles to meet employers’ needs.
atlas-vn.0104: DH student visa and residence card
atlas-vn.0105: A university authorised to take foreign students requests a DH entry visa, then a temporary residence card for the length of the course.
atlas-vn.0106: International students may not work at all, not even part time; private English lessons count, and lead to expulsion and a three-to-five-year ban.
atlas-vn.0110: Enrolled students with a three-way internship agreement are exempt from the work permit, but the host must obtain the exemption certificate and you need a DH visa. Graduates cannot intern: anything they do counts as ordinary work.
atlas-vn.0111: There is no job-search visa: when the student card expires you must leave, unless a work permit or exemption is approved first, which a graduate without two years of experience rarely gets.
atlas-vn.0112: Work permit and LĐ2 residence card
atlas-vn.0113: The employer advertises the job locally for five working days, then files the work permit with the provincial labour department; you enter on an LĐ2 visa, take a medical at an accredited Vietnamese hospital and get a two-year residence card. Contracts last two years at most.
atlas-vn.0114: Experts need a degree and two years of experience, one year in technology, digital, semiconductors, AI or finance.
atlas-vn.0116: Thesis research with a Vietnamese university uses a DH visa; researchers working with Vietnamese institutions without enrolling get an LV2 visa. Fieldwork, sampling or interviews need prior government clearance.
atlas-vn.0117: Scholarships are free of income tax, but universities cannot pay foreign PhD students a salary on a DH visa.
atlas-vn.0118: Vietnam has working-holiday agreements only with Australia and New Zealand; “teach and travel” offers on a tourist visa are illegal work.
atlas-vn.0120: British citizens and those of 18 EU countries, Italy, Germany, France and Spain among them, enter visa-free for 45 days, not extendable. Austria, Greece, Portugal, Ireland, the Baltic states, Malta and Cyprus need an e-visa of up to 90 days.
atlas-vn.0122: About two months ahead, have your degree, a foreign criminal record under 6 months old and work references legalised: since 11 September 2026 an apostille is enough for Italian documents, while some countries that objected still need consular legalisation.
atlas-vn.0123: On the e-visa, the order of your names must match the machine-readable line of your passport exactly, or the airline may refuse to board you.
atlas-vn.0124: Whoever houses you must register your temporary residence within 24 hours of arrival; otherwise you face fines of VND 3 to 5 million, and without the registration slip you cannot get the residence card.
atlas-vn.0125: A two-year temporary residence card for work (LĐ2) costs USD 145.
atlas-vn.0126: Register your employee tax code within 10 working days and join compulsory social and health insurance: 9.5% from you, 20.5% from the company.
atlas-vn.0127: Workers need a health check at an accredited Vietnamese hospital, about VND 1,500,000, for a certificate stating that they are fit for work.
atlas-vn.0128: Banks may not open accounts for tourist or e-visa holders. Professionals need a passport, a residence card valid at least 12 months, a work contract, a tax code and the residence slip, and must give biometrics in person; accounts freeze the day the card expires.
atlas-vn.0129: Whoever houses you must register you with the police within 24 hours; without it you cannot get a residence card.
atlas-vn.0130: Working before the work permit is issued means expulsion and a fine of up to 25 million VND.
atlas-vn.0131: Names on the e-visa must match the passport’s machine-readable line exactly, or airlines refuse boarding.
atlas-vn.0132: Banks cannot open accounts for tourists or e-visa holders, and need face biometrics in person.
atlas-vn.0133: A spouse’s family residence card gives no right to work.
atlas-vn.0134: Vietnam joined the Apostille Convention on 11 September 2026; provincial offices accept Italian apostilles unevenly.
atlas-vn.0135: Medical certificates from Italy are in practice rejected for the work permit.
atlas-vn.0136: Whether a visa-free visitor can switch to a work visa inside Vietnam is handled inconsistently.
